transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees (Redwood): Samir Patel (AE), Claire Wong (SE), Diego Ramos (notes)
Attendees (Customer): Laura Chen (Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Procurement), Evan Brooks (Security)

Summary:
Quick check-in to align on contract extension options and technical plan for EU private / APAC edge activation. Customer is evaluating a 12 vs 18 month extension, wants guaranteed regional capacity for Q4 ramp, and needs SOC2/KMS details for procurement. Action: SOW + benchmark pilot follow-up.

Topics flagged:
- Current usage and target throughput (tokens/month)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in EU
- Security/compliance (SOC2/KMS/SSO)
- Benchmarks for latency and throughput on their models
- Commercial term trade-offs and pricing tiers

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: all right everyone thanks for joining i think we've got a full house, um so quick agenda — commercial options, tech plan for eu onprem/private, and next steps. Laura, do you want to kick off with where you are on adoption?
[00:18] Laura: yeah thanks Samir, so quick recap we went live with the hosted APIs in Feb, baseline is about 95M tokens/month, production peak is around 12 rps for our summarization model. we expect to hit ~350M tokens by november with product rollout. procurement are asking for regional residency in eu for clinical notes and apac for training logs.
[00:36] Marco: and from infra perspective we need predictable capacity during peaks, we've hit a few throttles last quarter, so the dedicated/reserved option looks attractive but we need private deployment for data residency.
[00:49] Claire: okay, got it. two threads — one is capacity commit and burst model, second is private control plane / vpc. for capacity, we typically recommend reserved pool with burst to hosted for overflow. that keeps unit cost lower but keeps reliability.
[01:05] Laura: mhm, yes, cost is a concern though — CFO asked for per-token cost target around $0.0006 if we commit to 18 months, is that in scope?
[01:18] Samir: short answer yes we can run numbers. there are tradeoffs: longer term = better discount, private deployment has a premium for infra and support. we'll run three scenarios: 12m, 18m with reserved capacity, and 18m with partial dedicated + hosted overflow.
[01:33] Priya: procurement also needs SOC 2 type II evidence, and details on KMS/HSM for key custody if we do private. Evan, i'll flag security details.
[01:43] Evan: yeah we need to know how KMS integrates — customer-managed key vs redwood-managed, HSM options, and audit log retention for at least 2 years. also SSO via SAML and RBAC mapping for our teams.
[01:57] Claire: that makes sense. for private we support BYOK via KMS integration and can do HSM-backed keys in the private plane; audit logs can be exported to your log collector s3 or splunk. i'll drop the specific diagram, uh, the network flow, after this call.
[02:12] Marco: one more technical: model cold-start and kv-cache behavior. our models are Llama-v2 style fine-tuned variants, long context. we saw large token bill spikes due to repeated context. how does Redwood manage kv cache across private nodes?
[02:29] Claire: good q — we have prefix caching and sticky routing in the runtime. in private deployments we can configure longer cache TTLs and smarter shard placement. performance-wise, we should run an internal benchmark with your model profile to tune batch size and seq lengths.
[02:45] Diego: note — benchmark should measure p99 latency, throughput at 90th percentile of request distribution, and per-token cost.
[02:53] Laura: yes p99 and p50 matter, but we care about tail latency because some clinician flows are interactive. can you hit sub-200ms for short completions?
[03:03] Claire: for short completions on optimized kernels and half-precision quant we can get under 150-180ms on dedicated GPUs depending on batch sizing; we'll confirm in bench.
[03:15] Marco: also question — apac region, are you spinning up dedicated nodes or using cloud provider peering? we need low latency to sydney in production.
[03:25] Samir: APAC can be handled two ways: we have hosted nodes in major clouds (lower setup time), or we provision Dedicated pools in APAC as part of the reserved commitment. Private (on-prem) in APAC is more manual. We'll include timelines for both.
[03:40] Priya: can you clarify the SLA for dedicated vs hosted? we need 99.95% uptime for critical routing.
[03:48] Samir: Dedicated comes with SLA and predictable throughput; hosted has high availability but less guaranteed throughput SLAs. we'll call out the SLA numbers in the SOW.
[03:56] Laura: great. commercial question — if we expand mid-contract (like adding APAC mid-year), how does pricing adjust?
[04:05] Samir: standard amendment process — we can do a top-up addendum with pro-rated pricing. Often customers do a base reserved commitment and purchase burst capacity as needed. We'll include a sample amendment in the SOW.
[04:18] Evan: security redline — vendor cannot retain unencrypted clinical data in hosted logs. we need at-rest encryption + field-level redaction in transit.
[04:29] Claire: we can support field-level redaction at the proxy layer and ensure logs are encrypted. for hosted we can toggle retention to zero for sensitive fields. We'll document options.
[04:40] Laura: okay next — timeline ideally: we sign extension by early september, pilot benchmarks in late august, and eu private activation in october if all goes well. is that realistic?
[04:52] Samir: feasible but tight. bench week of Aug 24 is doable; SOW by Aug 20; legal loop needs to move quickly.
[05:01] Priya: legal note — target term 18 months but finance wants a 12-month fallback with renegotiation option at month 9. will you model that in the scenarios?
[05:10] Samir: yes we'll provide the 12m and 18m with break clauses and estimated cost deltas.
[05:16] Marco: for the bench can we do a hybrid — run the same harness against your hosted staging and our on-prem node so we can compare p99 tail behavior?
[05:25] Claire: absolutely, that's the plan. we'll coordinate infra access and test harness.
[05:29] Laura: perfect, last question — any competitive risk if we go multi-vendor? Anthropic was in RFP, but they don't have our private on-prem experience.
[05:38] Samir: noted — we'll include operational differentiators in the SOW and a short one-pager comparing expected unit economics.
[05:45] Diego: capture: benchmarks, SOW, network diagram, KMS details, legal redlines.
[05:49] Priya: yep.
[05:50] Samir: ok i'll summarize and follow up. thanks everyone.

Recap (end):
- Agreement to run pilot benchmark week of 2026-08-24 across hosted staging and customer on-prem.
- Redwood to deliver SOW with 12m vs 18m scenarios by 2026-08-20.
- Security to provide KMS/HSM integration options and network diagram by 2026-08-25.
- Customer to return legal redlines and preferred term by 2026-08-23.

References/links mentioned (represented as notes):
- SOW template (redwood/sow/v2) — Samir to attach in follow-up

End of transcript.
